topic: AI Coding Agent Code Index MCP Comparison 2026

competitors.title: AI Coding Context Tools Compared: Agents, Editors, MCPs & Sourcegraph
key_points: Frames the market as coding agents, context MCPs, code host MCPs, and Sourcegraph's code intelligence layer
Says coding agents rebuild understanding from scratch on each task and are limited to what they search
Positions Sourcegraph's SCIP indexing as structurally precise and cross-repository, not approximate embeddings
Calls Sourcegraph the best fit for enterprise-scale completeness such as migrations, audits, and large refactors
Exposes the code intelligence layer to any MCP-compatible agent through Sourcegraph's MCP server

competitors.title: CodeGraph
key_points: Pre-indexed code knowledge graph that auto-syncs on file changes and runs 100% locally
Promises surgical context with fewer tool calls, faster answers, and a single-call query path
Returns source, call paths, and blast-radius analysis from a graph of symbols, call edges, and dependencies
Targets multiple coding agents through MCP, including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and OpenCode
Emphasizes freshness through file watching and auto-sync instead of manual re-indexing

competitors.title: Claude Context
key_points: MCP plugin for semantic code search in Claude Code and other AI coding agents
Uses hybrid BM25 plus dense vector search to surface relevant code without multi-round discovery
Supports incremental indexing with Merkle trees so only changed files are re-indexed
Depends on a vector database plus embedding provider, which adds setup and infrastructure overhead
Aims to make an entire codebase available as context across millions of lines of code

competitors.title: CocoIndex Code
key_points: AST-aware semantic code search context that works with all coding agents
Claims 70% fewer tokens per turn and 80-90% cache hits on re-index
Uses Tree-sitter to chunk code by syntax and re-embed only changed files
Runs locally by default with no API key required, but can also use cloud providers
Offers CLI, MCP server, and Claude skill surfaces for the same shared index

competitors.title: Code execution with MCP: building more efficient AI agents
key_points: Shows MCP as a protocol layer that can be made more efficient by presenting servers as code APIs
Argues agents should load only the tools they need instead of shipping every tool definition into context
Highlights privacy-preserving operations where intermediate results stay in the execution environment by default
Frames code execution with MCP as a way to reduce token usage while handling more tools
Is useful as protocol-level context for comparing index servers versus execution-driven workflows

competitors.title: CLIs or MCP for Coding Agents? A Practical Comparison
key_points: Clarifies that CLIs shell out with commands while MCP exposes structured JSON-RPC style tools
Notes that major coding agents can use both CLIs and MCP in the same session
Argues that structured interfaces matter more as autonomous tasks get larger and more complex
Helps separate transport/protocol choice from the actual quality of the code index
Provides a useful framing for why MCP is a container, not the index itself

stats.fact: Sourcegraph says SCIP indexing is language-agnostic, updates incrementally, and is the only tool in its comparison with exhaustive coverage guarantees.
stats.source: Sourcegraph AI Coding Context Tools Compared

stats.fact: CodeGraph claims one tool call can return relevant source, call paths, and blast-radius analysis from a pre-built knowledge graph.
CodeGraph is positioned as 100% local, with no API keys and no external services.
CocoIndex Code claims about 70% fewer tokens per turn and 80-90% cache hits on re-index.
Claude Context uses hybrid BM25 + dense vector search and incremental indexing that only re-indexes changed files.
Claude Context requires a vector database plus embedding provider, which increases setup overhead relative to local-only tools.
Anthropic recommends presenting MCP servers as code APIs so agents load only the tools they need and keep intermediate results in the execution environment.
DeployHQ frames MCP as structured tool calls and says all major coding agents can use both MCP and CLIs in one session.
stats.source: DeployHQ CLIs or MCP for Coding Agents?

angles: The main divide is not MCP versus non-MCP, but approximate semantic retrieval versus structurally precise code graphs
MCP is only the transport layer; the real product difference is how each tool builds and refreshes codebase context
Local-first tools compete on token savings, freshness, and privacy, while enterprise tools compete on completeness and cross-repo coverage
Single-call graph answers are strong for blast-radius questions, while semantic search is stronger for fuzzy discovery
Setup burden matters: vector databases and embedding pipelines raise friction compared with local or shared daemon indexes
The best choice depends on whether the user needs single-repo help, multi-repo reasoning, or org-wide code intelligence
keywords: local code index for AI agents
outline: Introduction: why code indexes became the missing layer for AI coding agents in 2026
The comparison framework: agentic file exploration, semantic search, knowledge graphs, and code-host MCPs
Sourcegraph: precise SCIP indexing for cross-repo completeness
CodeGraph: local knowledge graph, auto-syncing, and one-call blast-radius answers
Claude Context: hybrid semantic retrieval with vector databases and incremental indexing
CocoIndex Code: AST-aware indexing, token savings, and shared indexes for teams
Protocol layer: what MCP changes, and what it does not change
CLI vs MCP vs code execution: where each approach fits in a coding agent stack
Trade-offs: precision, freshness, privacy, setup burden, and cost
Decision matrix: when to choose Sourcegraph, CodeGraph, Claude Context, or CocoIndex Code
Conclusion: code index choice is a product decision, not just an integration choice
